preamble: In Swedish and Norwegian retroflexion, /r/ followed by /d/ fuses with it into a single voiced retroflex stop [ɖ], and the [r] is no longer pronounced separately. This is cluster fusion (sandhi), part of the same pattern that gives [ʈ], [ɳ], [ɭ] and [ʂ] from /r/ + /t, n, l, s/. In Swedish it is regular in Central Standard Swedish but absent in Southern Swedish and other varieties with uvular r. In Norwegian, /rd/ gives [ɖ] only in some dialects, notably around Oslo; many native words with Old Norse -rð instead have [ɾ] or the retroflex flap [ɽ] (bord [buːɽ]).

examples.note: Retroflexion applies to the whole /rd/ cluster; not found in Southern Swedish with uvular r.
Listed as a pronunciation especially of the Oslo area; other dialects have [²fæːɭi], [fæːri] and similar forms.
Literary and loan words keep [ɾd] in many varieties; the fused [ɖ] is dialectal.
